page: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512gb is a memory-optimized server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 32 physical cores and 64 virtual CPUs via multithreading. The system is configured with 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of memory per core. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz and features a 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI.

Architectural tradeoffs include a shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention under sustained peak loads compared to dedicated-core instances. Additionally, local storage is limited to a minimal 1 GB network-attached volume, requiring external network storage solutions for any substantial data persistence. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external connectivity.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong memory and processing capabilities. It achieves top-tier status in PassMark CPU scores at 98,920.13 and database operations at 42,060.8. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 532.73 GB/sec and write speeds at 251.91 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also rank in the top tier, while Redis SET operations reach 111.5 million operations per second.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and shared CPU model, this server offers a cost-effective profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, exclusive CPU utilization. It is suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, data processing pipelines, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
